claims.text: The signature saba kuro-ni is simmered for two days in a tamari-based soy sauce (たまり醤油) rather than standard shoyu; this has not been confirmed as wheat-free by the restaurant and should not be assumed safe for celiac diners.

name: 蕎上人（駒形蕎上人） (Sobashonin (Komagata Sobashonin))

claims.text: The soba is served with a traditional kaeshi (soy-sauce-based tare) and bonito dashi; no gluten-free or wheat-free sauce alternative was mentioned in any available source.

name: ＆スリランカTOKYO（旧：RスリランカTOKYO） (& Sri Lanka Tokyo (formerly R Sri Lanka Toky)

claims.text: Curry is described as coconut-milk and spice based, served over rice rather than bread, and reportedly prepared without wheat flour or oil.

name: スタイルズケイクス＆カンパニー (Style's Cakes & Co.)

claims.text: Alongside its wheat-flour tarts, the shop offers a baked rice-flour donut (米粉の焼きドーナツ) as a wheat-free option on some days.

name: すごい煮干ラーメン凪 新宿ゴールデン街店本館 (Sugoi Niboshi Ramen Nagi — Shinjuku Golden G)

claims.text: The signature tare is a spiced sardine (iwashi)-based sauce; standard Japanese ramen tare of this type is soy-sauce based and contains wheat, though no source explicitly confirmed wheat content for this specific shop's tare.

name: スケマサ コーヒー (SUKEMASA COFFEE) (Sukemasa Coffee)

claims.text: The fruit sandwiches are built on fresh dairy whipped cream together with azuki (ogura-an) or white bean (shiro-an) paste, so the standard menu is not vegan; no dairy-free cream substitute was mentioned in any source.

name: 炭火串焼ヒヨク之トリ 水道橋店 (Sumibi Kushiyaki Hiyoku no Tori Suidobashi)

claims.text: All skewers, whether salt (shio) or sauce (tare) based, are grilled on the same shared binchotan charcoal grill, so cross-contact between wheat-containing tare and other skewers is likely; no dedicated gluten-free grilling process was found in any source.
The restaurant's tare glaze for yakitori is a traditional soy-sauce-based sauce, which in standard Japanese yakitori preparation contains wheat.
The restaurant highlights a strong ventilation/smoke-extraction system for the dining room, though this addresses odor/comfort rather than food allergens.

name: 炭火焼干物定食 しんぱち食堂 水道橋店 (Sumibiyaki Himono Teishoku Shinpachi Shokudo)

claims.text: Dried fish is grilled to order over charcoal rather than fried, and the menu emphasizes simple preparations (salt-grilled or dashi-based) rather than heavily sauced dishes, which may simplify identifying lower-risk items — though this has not been confirmed with staff.
